questions.q: Work out (−2)<sup>4</sup> × (−3)
Work out −5 − (−3)<sup>2</sup>
questions.ms: −14. (−3)² = 9, so −5 − 9 = −14. The minus outside the bracket is not squared.

questions.q: Round 0.06095 to 3 significant figures.
questions.ms: 0.0610. The first significant figure is the 6; the 9 rounds up, and the final 0 must stay to show 3 s.f.

questions.q: Work out an estimate for the value of 6.12 × 19.80.48
Without working them out, which of these has an answer greater than 35?
questions.ms: 35 ÷ 0.8. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer bigger; multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller.

questions.q:
You are given that 236 × 52 = 12 272.
Work out 2.36 × 5.2
questions.ms: 12.272. 2.36 has 2 decimal places and 5.2 has 1, so the answer has 3: 12 272 ÷ 1000.
23 600. 12 272 ÷ 52 = 236, and dividing by 0.52 (100 times smaller) gives an answer 100 times bigger.

questions.q: Write 900 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
questions.ms: 2² × 3² × 5². M1 a correct factor tree or repeated division, A1 index form.

questions.q: Use your answer to question 8 to explain why 900 is a square number.
questions.ms: B1 every power in 2² × 3² × 5² is even, so 900 = (2 × 3 × 5)² = 30².

questions.q: Write 900<sup>3</sup> as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2⁶ × 3⁶ × 5⁶. Cubing multiplies every power by 3: (2² × 3² × 5²)³. B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q:
84 = 22 × 3 × 7 and 140 = 22 × 5 × 7
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 140.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 84 and 140.

Amira has 60 red counters and 84 blue counters. She puts all of them into identical groups, with the same number of red counters and the same number of blue counters in each group, and none left over.
What is the greatest number of groups she can make?
questions.ms: 12 groups (5 red and 7 blue in each). M1 60 = 2² × 3 × 5 or lists factors, M1 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 or recognises HCF is needed, A1 12.
